textArea.b: Team 709 · Stemma, the family health tree

g.textArea: TECH 5900 Product Studio · Section 7 · Raj Kashikar · Viha Srinivas · Unser Jaffry
Oral review with our coach Oct 12–23, 2026 · one PDF due Oct 23, 2026 · analysis drafted Oct 6, 2026, revised after review and aligned with the final Maker Day 2 deck on Oct 12

The product in one line. With Stemma, a patient builds a three-generation family health tree before a first cardiology visit. Relatives can answer for themselves from a text link, on their phone, with no account; they can decline, or share one condition from their own patient portal (a public test server today). Every fact keeps who said it and a status in words: Known · Reports disagree · Unknown · Chose not to share · Not asked yet. The patient reviews a one-page summary, and the practice opens its own care-team copy by link or QR. Free for patients; practices pay, cardiology first: $1,000 for a 12-week pilot, credited to year one, then $500 per cardiologist a year.
Live prototype, synthetic data only: https://stemmahealth.vercel.app

How to read this. [n] is a numbered source in docs/research.md. [S#] is a source opened for the pitch work (Oct 6, 2026). Both lists, with URLs, are in the three Sources frames (see the board map). Interview IDs (ID002, ID006, ID007, ID010, D021) match the Team Hub "Interview Logs" (anonymized on the site's /research/interviews tab). Where this board quotes the Maker Day 2 deck (Google Slides 1JGhz-94qJGlWLe-9ZmBesYhjJp6ZIuggMYgFx6BK6kM, final Oct 12), it uses the slide's words exactly; slide numbers are the deck's (9 main slides, backup A0–A12). "(note)" means the note-taker's wording; words in quotation marks are only those the Team Hub notes put in quotation marks. Assumption marks our own estimate, with its math. Tags follow the course: N = new, O = old, N/O = some of each.

textArea.b: Step 4 verdict: Will people buy it?

g.textArea: Use: yes, if the practice sends the link. Buy: not yet shown. Patients gain the most against what they use today, and clinic-sent pre-visit tools get finished (57% of 95,166 invited finished one [92]). No practice manager, cardiologist or relative is among our 21 logged interviews, so payment and clinician value are unproven.

textArea.b: Step 5 verdict: Can we make it?

g.textArea: Yes at pilot scale, from about January 2027; not yet a business that pays salaries. The patient-to-clinician flow runs today on synthetic data; the pilot backend is next. Running it under BAAs costs about $689–834 a month. At $500 per cardiologist per year, 17–21 paying cardiologists cover that (9–11 groups of two); one developer's wage on top needs about 290, roughly every independent cardiologist in NYC. Founder support time (1–2 hours per practice a month) is unpaid and not in that cost.

cardiology guidelines need which relative and what age, intake forms take it from memory, and for $500 per cardiologist a year a practice-sent link puts those details, sourced, in the chart before visit one. (slide 9, word for word)

the patient side already runs on open health standards, a PDF reaches any chart, and a pilot on vendors that sign HIPAA contracts costs under $850 a month, which 17–21 paying cardiologists cover, founders unpaid. (slide 9, word for word)

Independent NYC cardiology groups (2–10 cardiologists) pay; their adult new patients use it free; relatives answer by link; the practice opens the care-team page by read-only link or check-in QR and files it as a PDF; a $1,000 12-week founding pilot credited to year one, then $500 per cardiologist per year.

3 independent NYC cardiology groups. Why cardiology first: its guidelines count grandparents, aunts and uncles, by side and age. Goal: 4 in 10 invited new patients have a reviewed page in the chart before visit one. (slide 9) In detail: groups of 2–10 cardiologists; all adult new patients (one link in the new-patient paperwork), sharpest for palpitations, fainting, chest pain or high cholesterol. The goal is measured on invited new patients whose first visit falls in pilot weeks 2–12, with a patient-reviewed summary in the chart before that visit (read at weeks 6 and 12; A11).

Any doctor who needs a family history, one specialty at a time: the rest of NYC's ~20 cardiology groups → larger groups → genetics and lipid clinics → primary care wellness visits. US independent cardiology alone: 7,699 cardiologists, $3.8M a year at $500. Markets beyond it are not yet sized. (slide 9) [99][104] Today only cardiology's questions and criteria are built.

$1,000 for a 12-week pilot, credited to year one, then $500 per cardiologist a year; free to patients (slide 3). $99 a month is a higher price we test on the same card; Step 5.3 also models $149 a month, our first guess, which is not on the card.

A practice pays $500 per cardiologist a year despite free intake tools. (slide 7; A3 shortens it to "a practice pays $500 per cardiologist a year"). 0 of 21 interviews were practice managers. Test by Oct 23: 5 practice-manager conversations with a one-page price card. Pass = 3 of 5 name the budget owner and accept $500/yr in principle, and 1 signs a non-binding letter of intent naming a target start month. The paid letter follows once we have a company, a BAA template and insurance.
